target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The diagnostic layer (`detectToolCallShapedText`) correctly classifies these JSON shapes, but the promotion layer (`parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks`) only recognizes bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats — leaving a gap where the system can see the tool call but cannot act on it.

This affects providers that route through `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) when the underlying model embeds tool calls in the assistant content as JSON objects. The reported symptom is the warning: "Assistant reply looks like a tool call, but no structured tool invocation was emitted; treating it as text."

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a new JSON-format parser (`parseJsonToolCallBlockAt`) into `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks`, matching the same 4 JSON shapes already classified by `classifyJsonValue` in `tool-call-shaped-text.ts`:

1. `{"tool_calls": [...]}` — OpenAI wrapper format
2. `{"function": {"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}}` — nested function format
3. `{"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}` — flat format
4. `{"name": "...", "type": "tool_call", ...}` — explicit type format

The existing safety gates are preserved: `allowedToolNames` whitelist filtering (only registered tool names are promoted) and the standalone-only invariant (the entire text must be consumed by tool-call blocks — no mixed prose). Stringified arguments (`"arguments": "{\"x\":1}"`) are handled via `JSON.parse` normalization.

This is the correct ownership boundary because `tool-call-repair` is the canonical location for text-to-tool-call promotion, and all providers using `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` automatically benefit.

## User Impact

Affected: users routing tool-calling agents through local/proxy providers (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) with models that serialize tool calls as JSON text in `content` rather than through native `tool_calls` fields (observed with Qwen family models).

After fix: these JSON-embedded tool calls are correctly parsed and promoted into executable tool calls, matching the behavior already present for bracket/XML/Harmony text formats.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload` — 22 passed
- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared` — 66 passed
- `pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/stream` — 16 passed
- Lint clean: `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`
- Format check: `oxfmt --check` passes

Behavior addressed: JSON-format plain-text tool calls are now promoted to executable tool calls, closing the gap between the diagnostic layer (which already recognized them) and the promotion layer (which previously did not).

Environment: standard Linux dev checkout, Node 22.

Commands run after this patch:
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts
pnpm format:check packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts
```

Evidence after fix: all 22 + 66 + 16 tests pass, lint and format clean.

Observed result after fix: JSON-format tool-call text blocks are correctly parsed and promoted through the same path as bracket/XML/Harmony formats.

What was not tested: live end-to-end reproduction with a real Ollama instance and Qwen model, due to no local Ollama setup available. The behavioral gap is verified at the source level: `classifyJsonValue` recognizes these 4 shapes, and the new `parseJsonToolCallBlockAt` matches the same recognition logic for promotion.
